findings.title: Toolchain directory mode contract is incompatible with ordinary provider
findings.observation: namespace_argv requires private_directory(toolchain), exactly0700. Existing _toolchain rejects mode &0o277, including owner-write, so0700 is rejected and a valid private read-only0500 root is accepted by the provider but rejected by layout. The two mode sets are disjoint. Synthetic controls always manufacture0700 toolchain roots and miss this.
findings.next_action: Use a separate owned/canonical/read-only managed-toolchain validator matching current _toolchain semantics; keep private_directory for writable work. Add a0500 positive and0700 negative provider/layout control. Do not chmod the installed toolchain or relax its provider merely to satisfy layout.

findings.title: Code generation recheck accepts unlisted mounted members
findings.observation: After stage_code, adding unindexed.py succeeds through namespace_argv. It validates only staged.files, but ro-binds the entire directory. The mounted code generation can therefore include unpinned files/subdirectories/symlinks. This probe does not demonstrate untrusted control over the parent work directory; it demonstrates the advertised generation drift check is incomplete.
findings.next_action: Before emitting argv, enumerate the exact allowed regular files and necessary ancestor directories without following symlinks. Refuse additions, unexpected types, or missing members; retain hashes, ownership, nlink and directory checks. Add extra-file and extra-symlink negatives.

findings.title: Layout does not exclude writable alias of nested toolchain
findings.observation: namespace_argv accepts toolchain=work/toolchain. The argv ro-binds it at PREFIX while the whole work tree is writable at WORK; the same assets then have writable WORK/toolchain aliases. No actual namespace was run. This requires an invalid internal layout choice, rather than an attacker-controlled ordinary provider path.
findings.next_action: Reject toolchain==work and toolchain descendants of writable work; preferably reject either tree overlap as the installed/work topology invariant. Preserve the fixed installed provider boundary and add a nested/equal negative.
